messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD#INC-9012) — inference-queue latency spike + queue-depth > 15k across hotpath. Trigger: queue_length_threshold (>= 10000)

pagerduty-bot: page: INC-9012 -> eng-oncall (severity: P1) — auto-escalation in 8m if unacked. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-9012

alice: acked via PD, I'm on it. seeing large tail latencies on /v1/generate and 5xx surge in gateways (502/504). dashboards show 99th p90 -> 12s.

bhaskar: looking at autoscaler logs — scale-controller shows repeated `NodePoolPending` counts then abort because cloud provider returns 429. suspecting kube API rate limiting + spot inventory drop.

carla: can anyone confirm spot preemption wave? cloud console shows spot eviction rate ~28% in us-west1. reserved pools are at capacity.

diego: reproducing scale controller log snippet:```
2026-03-15T03:07:12Z scale-controller INFO pending_pods=3120
2026-03-15T03:07:13Z cloud-api WARN create-instance failed status=429 body="Rate exceeded"
2026-03-15T03:07:14Z scale-controller ERROR reconcile_failed reason="double-counted_pods"
```

alice: whoa — `double-counted_pods` is a newish metric from the last runtime patch (v0.9.3). Could be race between pending->creating transition. That would make the autoscaler think it's scaled when it's not.

oncall-lead: @carla @bhaskar escalate to SRE and infra — this is customer impacting. PD page has been acked by Alice but we need ownership.

bhaskar: assigning to @diego (infra) and @carla (sre). immediate mitigations I'm proposing: 1) toggle fallback routing to dedicated pool 2) manual scale of reserved nodepool 3) temporarily increase kube-apiserver client QPS.

carla: doing 1) now — flipping feature flag `fallback_to_dedicated` to on for inference-route. Command: `redwoodctl feature set fallback_to_dedicated=true --scope=global`

carla: done. quick check: traffic % to dedicated jumped to ~18% and those requests have p50~190ms. overall 95th latency dropping slightly.

diego: doing 2) manual scale: `redwoodctl nodepool scale --pool=reserved-hot --count=8 --reason="PD INC-9012 emergency"` — cloud API still returning 429 on some attempts, but 4 nodes provisioned successfully, 4 pending.

diego: also opened a support ticket with cloud provider (case #CP-4421) — high spot churn + API throttling.

alice: customer-facing note: some customers see degraded generative responses and timeouts; we've rerouted high-risk traffic to dedicated nodes to reduce impact. will prepare status update.

bhaskar: temporary autoscaler knob: setting `scale_controller.acknowledge_double_count=true` to bypass the new safety check while we diagnose. applying now.

carla: applied. scale-controller logs show new reconciles creating more instances. queue depth dropped from 15k -> 6.5k in 7m.

diego: follow-up: root cause candidate = race in scale controller introduced in v0.9.3 when both controller and kubelet update pod state; combined with cloud API 429s the controller marked pending pods as created prematurely. will revert patch or patch logic.

oncall-lead: escalate notes: 1) continue manual scale until cloud provider stabilizes 2) remove `acknowledge_double_count` after patch fix 3) postmortem owner: @diego 4) customer comms: @alice to draft.

alice: drafting status update now: "We've detected autoscaler under-provisioning due to scale-controller and cloud API throttling; mitigations in flight (reroute + manual scaling). No data loss, partial degraded latency for some customers. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

pagerduty-bot: PD note: INC-9012 acked by alice at 4832101248. escalation to SRE team initiated at 4832101254.

incident-bot: added incident ticket: INC-9012 -> /incidents/9012. severity: P1. playbook invoked: autoscale-fallback.

carla: quick smoke checks: run `curl -I https://api.redwood.example/v1/health` from edge — all OK, but `/v1/generate` 95th still elevated in some regions.

bhaskar: any sign of thermal issues on GPUs? monitoring shows GPU temp spikes on a subset of older nodes; combined with spot churn that might explain node rejection. opening hw ticket but not primary.

diego: next steps: push hotfix to scale-controller that rechecks instance create status and on 429s retries with exponential backoff + idempotent pod counting. will stage canary in us-west1-only.

oncall-lead: good. keep thread updated. I'll prep rotation for handoff in 30m if still active. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alice: posting status to #status-page in 10m. thanks team.

carla: note for postmortem: improve runbook to include immediate `redwoodctl nodepool scale` and toggling fallback flag; also add cloud API throttling detection signal to alert earlier.
